verses.1:
Of David. A Maskil. + 32:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142. 
 Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven,
 whose sins are covered. + 32:1 LXX Blessed is he whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered ; cited in Romans 4:7|ROM 4:7
verses.2:
Blessed is the man
 whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him, + 32:2 LXX Blessed is the man whose sin the LORD does not count against him ; cited in Romans 4:8|ROM 4:8 
 in whose spirit there is no deceit.
verses.3:
When I kept silent, my bones became brittle
 from my groaning all day long.
verses.4:
For day and night
 Your hand was heavy upon me;
 my strength was drained + 32:4 Or my vitality was turned 
 as in the summer heat.
 Selah
verses.5:
Then I acknowledged my sin to You
 and did not hide my iniquity.
 I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,”
 and You forgave the guilt of my sin.
 Selah
verses.6:
Therefore let all the godly pray to You
 while You may be found.
 Surely when great waters rise,
 they will not come near.
verses.7:
You are my hiding place.
 You protect me from trouble;
 You surround me with songs of deliverance.
 Selah
verses.8:
I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go;
 I will give you counsel and watch over you.
verses.9:
Do not be like the horse or mule,
 which have no understanding;
 they must be controlled with bit and bridle
 to make them come to you.
verses.10:
Many are the sorrows of the wicked,
 but loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD.
verses.11:
Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous ones;
 shout for joy, all you upright in heart.
